draft.title: Logarithmic scales
card: On an ordinary scale, equal steps add the same amount. On a logarithmic scale, equal steps multiply the quantity by the same factor.
The Richter scale for earthquakes is logarithmic. Each increase of 1 in magnitude multiplies the measured ground shaking by 10.
The decibel (dB) scale for sound intensity is logarithmic too. Each increase of 10 dB multiplies the sound intensity by 10.
Example: a rise of 2 on the Richter scale means 10 × 10 = 100 times the shaking.
draft.remember: On a logarithmic scale, going up one step multiplies the quantity. It does not add to it.

a.q: One earthquake measures 4 on the Richter scale and another measures 6. How many times greater is the measured shaking of the second?
a.why: The scale rises by 2 steps, and each step multiplies the shaking by 10. So the shaking is 10 × 10 = 100 times greater. Saying 10 times counts only one step.
a.clue: Count the steps, then multiply by 10 for each.

b.q: A quiet room has sound at 30 dB. A busy street measures 60 dB. How many times greater is the sound intensity on the street?
b.why: The rise is 30 dB, which is three steps of 10 dB. Each step multiplies the intensity by 10, so 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 times. Saying 2 times divides the readings, and 100 times counts only two steps.
b.clue: Each 10 dB is one step, so count the steps first.
